examples.en: Everyone praises her cooking.
He's always boasting about his new car.

tips: With the reflexive particle, «хвалити се» means to boast, usually + instr.: «хвали се успехом». Without «се» it means to praise someone.

examples.en: A strong earthquake hit the south of the country.
We felt a weak earthquake last night.
I envy you that vacation.
Everyone envies his success.

note: person + dat., thing: на + loc.: «завидим ти на успеху»
tips: Завидети + dat.: «Завидим ти на свему». The noun is завист. Not to be confused with љубомора - jealousy, the wish to have someone all to yourself.

examples.en: Cover yourself with a blanket, it's cold.
Bring one more blanket.

tips: Ћебе is a thin blanket (often wool); a quilt with filling in a duvet cover is јорган.
The plural is irregular: ћебад (not ћебета): «топла ћебад». Same pattern: ја́гње - јагњад, дете - деца.

examples.en: The Royal Guard protects the court.

The project ended in failure.

examples.sr: Могу ли да те [помо̀лим] за услугу?

examples.sr: Бака је [помо̀лила] комшију да јој помогне.
examples.en: Grandma asked the neighbor to help her.

note: «помолити се» - to pray

examples.en: The police caught a dangerous bandit.

The police suspected the neighbor.

note: Often «forest» in Serbia; for «mountain» планина is more common.

examples.en: I have to renew my passport.

forms: gen. муслимана; pl. муслимани; f. муслиманка

note: «сунчан дан» - a sunny day; «сунчев» - of the Sun

examples.sr: Деца су [ра̀њива] и треба их штитити.

note: usually a noun: «преживели» - the survivors

examples.sr: Позвали су га у [ту̀жила̄штво] на разговор.

He speaks Turkish.

note: written with a lowercase letter (unlike English)

note: «истерати своје» - to get one's way

note: + dat.

note: usually «доселити се»

note: mostly plural: «манири» - manners
